Dear Community and lavaan experts,

I am trying to fit a Second-Order Multi-Group Latent Change Model for 3 time-points and 4 groups using the "growth"-function to assess personality development of trait Extraversion.

For each time point, I have created 3 parcels serving as indicators for latent trait Extraversion (due to number of items, 4 parcels are not possible).
The item scale ranges from 1-7.
To keep strong measurement invariance for time points, I fixed corresponding parcel loadings and intercepts (see model below).
To additionally explain variance in the second order latent slope and intercept factor, I regressed them on one (continuous) covariate measured at T1.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Second-Order Multi-Group Latent Growth Model: Model fitting issues
parts: how can the parcel-intercepts be higher than the maximum of the scale (7)?

An endogenous variable's intercept is its estimated marginal mean when each of its predictors == 0.  If your indicator intercepts are outside the range of observed values, then 0 is probably outside the range of values for its predictor(s).  In this case, the only predictor of each indicator is its common factor, and the common factors all have means of 0.998 (at T1) or greater (because the slope is positive, as are the slope loadings for T2 and T3).  Given how small the variances are for the common factors, a value of 0 would be many SDs below the mean, so the intercepts for the indicators are the conditional means of those variables for very atypical values on the common factors.
Shouldn't the Second Order Intercept be in range of the population mean (which is around 3.5), but not near zero?

Not necessarily.  First, you used the identification constraint of fixing the common-factor intercepts to zero.  If you used a marker variable to identify the mean structure (i.e., fixing the first indicator's intercept == 0), like you did for the covariance structure (i.e., fixing the first indicator's loading == 1), then your model-implied latent means should be in the familiar 1-7 range (not that those variables would be on a 1-7 scale).  But the estimated growth-factor intercepts might still be outside that range, depending on the observed values of the covariate that predicts the growth factors.  Again, an endogenous variable's intercept is its estimated marginal mean when each of its predictors == 0.  So if zero is outside the range of observed values for the covariate, then the growth-factor intercepts are conditional on values that do not apply to your sample.  To solve that "problem", you could center the covariate at a meaningful value, or the minimum observed value, or the mean.
Several negative variances in several groups show that something is wrong with my model. But what? Is the number of observations to small?

Possibly related to the hidden proportionality assumption in the latent-basis curve.  It is not as "unrestricted" as people think:

http://dx.doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2014.938578
Or is this more a question for SEMNET?
SEMNET would be a good place to post questions like this, because they are not software-specific.
Is it possible to manually set parameters equal for specific groups (e.g. group 1 and 2) but not for others using the "group.equal" comand?

No, that is just a shortcut.  Better to specify constraints manually with labels in the syntax

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/syntax2.html

Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
